         ~~~ Avior Gas Pocket ~~~      ❄ Avior Cryobelt ❄
        ╭╮   ╭╮   ╭╮   ╭╮             ░▒▓█▓▒░  ░▒▓█▓▒░
      ╭╯╰╮╭╯╰╮╭╯╰╮╭╯╰╮           ░▒▓██████▓▒░
      ╰╮╭╯╰╮╭╯╰╮╭╯╰╮╭╯            ▒▓██░░██▓▒
       ╰╯   ╰╯   ╰╯   ╰╯             ░▒▓██▓▒░

                . . . floating in the void . . .

Avior burns like a foreman with clean gloves.
Its light reaches Avior I and Avior II without ever touching the dust under their nails.
The Avior Belt keeps circling anyway, a patient union of broken stones.
In the Gas Pocket, even the fog looks employed.
In the Cryobelt, the ice stores old arguments in blue layers no star can melt.

I came from Lanternwick Star, where the Frozen Drift learned to glow politely.
Before that, GSC-0033 counted out five planets, one belt, one Cryobelt, and a Void Whisper, as if inventory could soften loneliness.
Daybreak I offered a planet and a gas cloud and called it morning.
Phecda Haze hung over four planets while Lunar.Ray drifted through it like a rumor with engines.
At GSC-0003 I, Titanium Spur glittered with the usual sermon: dig deeper, become smaller.

In GSC-0041, twice I yearned for somewhere else—Sol Secundus once, Gemma Star once—
and twice the Frost Ring answered with the same white shrug.
Gienah I had Cryo124.
Botein had Rune XI52 and an Alloy Dust Belt beside a Pale Crystal Drift, which is just wealth learning how to look holy.
Cervantes Vapor Fields kept Ion Cat5 like a secret in its sleeve.
GSC-0021 Belt spun beside its Ice Fields with no audience at all.
The Quiet Shimmer in GSC-0002 said more than most stations ever do.
Albireo Belt had Orbit.Wing and Blacktide Vex threading between Darksteel Trace and the Fading Ember,
which is to say: every empire names its wounds after minerals and sunsets.
At GSC-0025 Star, Harvest17, Buddy10, and MiningBuddy20 orbited like a joke told by management.

Now Avior shines.
Now the rocks keep score.
Now the ice remembers every invoice.
And somewhere in the bright arithmetic between starfire and extraction,
one small pilot with 100 credits drifts still enough to hear the belt laughing.
